methods.label: Find the next palindrome
methods.sourceMethod: Use the leading digits to construct the next palindrome, then divide the mileage increase by elapsed time.

annotationRationale: The matching-digit constraint and place-value order determine the least larger palindrome. The mileage difference and elapsed time then determine average speed.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate for decimal digit reasoning and an elementary speed calculation. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The next palindrome is \(16061\), giving \((16061-15951)/2=55\) miles per hour, choice B. The question, choices and recorded answer agree. No figure is supplied or needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both supplied references use the same digit-order construction followed by average speed. The AoPS carry explanation is a variation of this route, so no additional method is needed.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed roles for constrained digit deduction and the distance-speed-time relationship are appropriate. Decimal place value and inverse arithmetic are reasonable supporting concepts. All candidate IDs have supplied definitions.
review.areaCheck: Prealgebra is appropriate for decimal digit reasoning and an elementary speed calculation. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: A five-digit palindrome is uniquely fixed by its first three digits. Prefix 159 forces the original reading; the least larger prefix is 160, which forces 16061. Larger prefixes give larger readings, establishing minimality. The distance is \(110\) miles and the average speed is \(110/2=55\) miles per hour.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited sources support the claimed construction and speed calculation. They are correctly treated as nonofficial third-party references through source-informed-original. The candidate adds an independently phrased explanation of matching digits and minimality, without copied sentences or sentence-by-sentence paraphrase.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening digit example motivates using the leading digits. The explanation then justifies why the next prefix gives the next palindrome and clearly connects odometer subtraction to distance and division by time to average speed. All transitions are accessible at AMC 10 level.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four immediate nodes fit: finite-constraint deduction covers forced mirrored digits and the least permitted prefix; cnm_p096 supplies decimal place value; cnm_p111 supplies the distance-speed-time relationship; cnm_p110 supports recovering distance and speed through inverse operations.
